claims.claim: A drop ('צניחה') in the number of sexual-assault investigations under Trump
claims.verified_figure: U.S. Education Dept. OCR (federal civil-rights / Title IX administrative probes of schools): 'dozens' of sexual-violence investigations opened per year before the March 2025 layoffs vs 'fewer than 10 nationwide' opened since (AP, internal OCR data, 2026-01-16). Related: zero sexual-violence/harassment cases resolved by agreement in 2025; Title IX resolution agreements 80 (2024) -> 31 (2025).
claims.note: Article body unreachable (EGRESS_BLOCKED + premium paywall); judged the headline only. The direction and magnitude ('plunge') are supported by the AP/OCR data, but the headline omits which body and what kind of investigation: the documented drop is in federal Education Dept. OCR Title IX administrative investigations of schools, not criminal sexual-assault investigations (police/DA/FBI/DOJ), which is the natural Hebrew reading of 'חקירות התקיפה המינית'. No baseline period or count is given, and the underlying AP dataset is non-public ('dozens' vs '<10' is itself vague). The Cornell case does not itself evidence the national trend — the criminal probe there was a local DA decision in 2024 (pre-Trump), now reopened by NY AG — but that causal framing ('מצביעה') is editorial and not separately verdicted. If the body specifies OCR/Title IX, the body is likely accurate; cannot verify.
